mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays sharply below baseline, weekday trips remain suppressed and spill over into discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC should stay lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean for the next 28 days while WORKPLACES remains below baseline for most weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week drop in RESIDENTIAL below its recent level indicates more time spent outside home, which converts into more shopping and dining visits within two weeks, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5% above baseline after being at or above 5% for the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL crosses down through the 5%-above-baseline threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall in the same week, access to central retail districts weakens and retail visits decline over the next one to four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are below their own prior-week values.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after a prior dip signals improved outdoor conditions and weekend mobility, which should lift adjacent discretionary shopping within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 15 points week-on-week from a negative reading
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following 7 days after PARKS increases by 15 points or more from below zero.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains far below baseline while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, restrictions or caution keep people local and suppress mall and high-street trips, so retail mobility falls over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -40 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +5 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior four-week mean despite two consecutive weeks of low TRANSIT and elevated RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run rise in GROCERY_PHARM absorbs some out-of-home errands into essential trips, crowding out discretionary retail visits and pushing RETAIL_REC down within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM turns positive after being negative in the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM crosses from negative to positive year-over-year change.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both move up together, households are substituting toward home-and-local recreation, which leaves less demand for retail districts over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not underperform its prior 28-day mean when both PARKS and RESIDENTIAL are above their recent averages.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates reopening of commuting networks; retail spending follows with a lag, so RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week average over the next 28 days when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES trend upward together.
